rows.why: He was talking about his brother's daughters (benat akhui, plural) but used the singular she/you form bitilbis; Amal echoed تلبس؟ and he restarted with bilbesu (they wear) in the same second.

rows.medi_said: سجاد طيارة أو طيا-- س-سجاد بطير.
rows.amal_said: مم. بيطير. [تضحك] يعني راح تعملوا حفلة؟
rows.why: He used the I-form بطير for a carpet that flies; Amal recast بيطير (it flies) and he repeated بي-بي-ب-بطير after her.
He put the owner ending on the first word and the word order reversed (birthday = 'eid miilaad', thing first then owner ending); Amal recast عيد ميلاده and he repeated عيد ميلادو.
Amal had just offered بكون عنا (ykoon for the habitual, 3ind + we); he said بيكون with أنا as the subject, not matching 'we have a party', and she let it pass with mm-hmm.

rows.medi_said: مش أمل party. أمل؟ مش، مش أمل party.
rows.amal_said: مم. Why miss-- No miss. Why miss? ... ما عمل.
rows.why: Engine wrote أمل but Amal's reply 'No miss... ما عمل' shows he said mish 3amal (a verb) and she wanted ma before the verb; he then said ما أمل party at 11:14.
rows.english: He did not make a party

rows.why: He gave the date with el- (الثلاثين) and Amal answered with the bare date form صار تلاتين; could also just be her acknowledgement.

rows.medi_said: الـ card بس نسيت ... خلصته، خلصتهم.
rows.why: After نسيت he put the second verb in the past (خلصته); Amal named the rule 'Second verb present' and gave أخلصه.

rows.amal_said: أنا راح أحكي لك. We don't, we don't say just I will.
rows.why: He stopped at ra7 with no verb; Amal gave the whole sentence and said you don't say just 'I will'.

rows.medi_said: أوكي، أنا راح أشوفك. أنا راح أحكيلك.
rows.why: The thing to see was the homework (شوفه), but he put the you ending (أشوفك = I will see you); Amal said No and then 'Nice. Well done' for the rest. The No could also be about the أنا راح أحكيلك repeat, which is less likely.
rows.english: I will see it, I will tell you

rows.why: English/French word dropped into an Arabic sentence; sheet row: 'pants | Ban6aloan | بنطلون | ban6aloan' (pre-ruled: do not correct, AR-1933).
He was reaching for 'dark' (pantalon سيكني ... dark), said an unclear word three times and Amal supplied غامق; sheet: 'dark (color) | 8aameq | غامق'.
Amal asked what he expects to take; he said 'nobody' (حدا = someone) when the thing 'nothing' was needed, she replied ولا إشي and he repeated it (sheet: 'nothing | Wala eshi').
He used ل with كباب after نعزم; Amal said على and then 'invite to. Did we review invite to?' (عزم على).
rows.english: invite my fiancée's family to kebab

rows.amal_said: No. ... You invite people to the wedding.
rows.why: He put the person ending on the preposition (عليهم); Amal said No and he rebuilt it as بعزم حدا على (the person is the verb's object, على goes with the event).
He was answering 'invite people to your wedding' and said عروس (bride); sheet: 'wedding | 3urus | عرس' vs 'bride | 3aroos | عروس'. Amal moved on without comment (could be the engine).
'I get happy' needs the n- form (بنبسط); he said the make-happy form ببسط, Amal said No and he retried bandaset.
He said 'my fiancée's daughters'; Amal echoed it laughing 'Already?' and he fixed to بنات أخوي (his brother's daughters) at 24:47. Slip of the tongue rather than a missing word.

rows.medi_said: بنمسد tilha for her. I don't know. لما، لما تخلص المدرسة.
rows.why: He built the preposition + her as tilha; Amal recast بنبسط لها. Her recast may also be aimed at the verb (he said بنمسد, S4), so only the preposition part is filed.

rows.medi_said: أنا بنمسد بي آخد، uh, سورة. Or بسورة.
rows.amal_said: Did we say, did we take the noun for s-photography? تصوير. ... بالتصوير. التصوير. ... Because you can't add be to a verb.
rows.why: He put a verb phrase (take a picture) after بـ; Amal prompted for the noun, gave تصوير, and said 'you can't add be to a verb. It would have to be a noun.'
Asked what prepositions بنبسط takes, he listed bi, la, ala; Amal echoed هلا and began another word and he said 'Min, sorry. Bi, la, and min'. Engine writes Latin here.

rows.medi_said: No, I'm not-- I'm trying to remember the, the adjective right now ... Does it start with an S-H?
rows.why: Amal asked for the verb 'to miss' and its adjective; he could not recall them, she supplied بستاق and finally مشتاق.

rows.medi_said: I'm guessing there is a preposition because of this lesson. أنا بشتا عليك.
rows.why: Amal echoed عليك? and said No to 'is that right?'; the correct partner is ل (she later says بشتاق لك / مشتاق لك).

rows.medi_said: أنا بكون مشتاق. No, that doesn't sound--
rows.amal_said: No. Bakoon, you didn't get habitual or conditional. So it's just now, I miss you.
rows.why: He used bakoon for a plain present state; Amal said no, bakoon is for habitual/conditional, so just أنا مشتاق.

rows.amal_said: اشتقت. No al in the middle.
rows.why: For 'I missed (you)' he put ع in the middle (شتعلت); Amal gave اشتقت (ق) and said no al in the middle. Could be read as an S4 root-letter slip but he kept شتعلت after her fix (39:00, 39:04).

rows.medi_said: What's I excite? Uh, أنا بتحمس.
rows.amal_said: Mm-hmm. بحمس. بحمس. أنا، أنا بتحمس.
rows.why: Asked for 'I excite' (make-X) he gave the get-excited form بتحمس; Amal said بحمس twice and contrasted with أنا بتحمس; he answered 'What'd I say?' so he did not hear the difference.

rows.medi_said: أنا بتحمس، uh، شهر الماضي عشان
rows.amal_said: Wait. Do you mean next month for the next month? ... الشهر الجاي.
rows.why: He said 'last month' (الماضي) for 'next month'; Amal asked 'Do you mean next month?' and he fixed to للشهر الجاي, she confirmed الشهر الجاي.

rows.medi_said: the holidays, would you guys say Eid? La Eid? Okay. عشان الـ Eid.
rows.why: He asked whether to say Eid and then put English Eid inside the Arabic clause; Amal answered with العيد (a didn't-know rather than a slip).

rows.amal_said: وصل-- 'cause you used بيتك so make it gender appropriate.
rows.why: Asked 'what time did you arrive home yesterday?' to Amal, he used the masculine you ending وصلت; she said make it gender appropriate and he fixed to وصلتِ.

rows.amal_said: أؤذ حالي؟ ... Uh, that doesn't really work. ... Yes، 'cause it's مؤذ.
rows.why: For 'I cut myself' he used a verb Amal says is for cutting with scissors (snip snip); she said it doesn't work but did not give the right word. Engine may have written 'مؤذ' for 'مقص'.

rows.medi_said: Is it I ge- I get annoyed is أنا بأذ, right?
rows.amal_said: I annoy. أنا بأزعج. ... Mm. No, no, no, it's an N verb.
rows.why: He gave the make-annoy form for 'I get annoyed'; Amal said بأزعج is 'I annoy' and it's an N verb (بنزعج); engine garbles the verb itself (بأذ).

rows.medi_said: أنا بتعب زيادة لما، أتمرن أو أشتغل، uh، نفس اليوم. The same day.
rows.amal_said: Great job. بس make it on the same day or in the same day.
rows.why: He said the same day with no preposition; Amal asked him to make it 'on / in the same day' and he fixed it to بنفس اليوم.

rows.amal_said: You're angry at him because he's annoyed? ... Or because he's annoying. Nice.
rows.why: He said 'annoyed' (مزعوج) when he meant 'annoying'; Amal asked it back in English and he fixed to مزعج, she said Nice.

rows.medi_said: ما تأسب عليني. ما تأسب عليني. علي.
rows.why: He put a verb pronoun ending (-ني) on the preposition (عليني); Amal recast علي and he repeated علي. The engine may have written -ني for his hesitation.

rows.medi_said: أنا بتضايق على الزباين لما متأخر كتير.
rows.amal_said: That's, that's you're sad for them. ... أنا بزعل من أو بدايق.
rows.why: He wanted 'upset with customers when they're late' but used على (= pity/sad for them); Amal said that means you're sad for them and gave من, he said 'you're right'.
rows.english: I get upset with customers when they are very late

rows.amal_said: بعدين لما takes-- لما is conditional so what does it take؟ ... يكونوا متأخرين.
rows.why: After لما he went straight to the adjective with no verb 'be'; Amal asked what لما takes, he said Akoun, and she gave يكونوا متأخرين.
He negated 3ind with مش; Amal recast ما عند and he repeated ما عند Halloween.
Asked for the command 'be upset', he said a word Amal echoed as واقفة (stop); he said 'that's stop' and self-fixed to إتضايق after her question. Engine may have garbled the first word.

rows.medi_said: أنا بفضل إشي أكثر من إشي.
rows.why: He used 'more than' for 'prefer X over Y'; Amal said 'That's more than' and he moved to على (قهوة على شاي) which she then used.
Both nouns are the known things (coffee over tea in general) and need el-; Amal recast with القهوة / الشاي and he said 'Gosh darn it'.

rows.medi_said: أنا قهوة، uh, المفضل إشي عندي
rows.amal_said: آه، اسمع عمرك. Have you ever tried the Arabic coffee؟
rows.right: القهوة المفضلة عندي / إشي المفضل عندي
rows.why: The adjective مفضل comes before its noun and with no noun matched; mufaddal follows its noun (A23). Amal let it pass and changed the subject.
Preferring latte over black coffee ('the black one') should take el- on the second noun like القهوة على الشاي just before; Amal let it pass. Engine is garbled here (على сода).
The verb after لازم keeps its b- (برجع) instead of dropping it (أرجع); Amal only corrected the preposition after كباب later. Engine may have written برجع for أرجع.
rows.english: Tomorrow I have to go back home
